hindi: जिस स्त्री के लिए पुष्प यानी सम्भवतः रज का आना उचित हो, गर्भ के जातसार यानी सार प्राप्त कर चुकने पर, त्याज्य बातों का त्याग न करने से पुष्प का दर्शन हो, या योनि से कोई और स्राव हो।
english: In her for whom the puṣpa (the 'flower': probably menstrual-type bleeding) is due (arhati), the fetus (garbha) having acquired its essence (jātasāra), through non-avoidance of the things to be avoided there may be the sight of puṣpa, or some other flow from the yoni (vagina).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit (yasyāḥ here, tasyāḥ in 42); the sentence is left open. 'puṣpa' (flower) is an idiom for menstrual-type bleeding (probable, as in the earlier chunk). The sense of 'puṣpam arhati' is not firm: arhati is taken as 'is fit/due' with puṣpa as its subject; the line may also mean 'who is fit for puṣpa' (i.e. of menstruating age). jātasāra: the fetus whose sāra (essence, firmness) has arisen; not enriched. 'anyat ... yonisravaṇam' read as 'or another flow from the yoni'.
lines_deva: यस्याः पुष्पमर्हति जातसारे गर्भे वर्ज्यानामवर्जनात्पुष्पदर्शनं स्यादन्यद्वा योनिस्रवणं

hindi: उसके लिए उसी कारण से कुपित वायु यानी वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा यानी कफ को पकड़कर, गर्भ की रस यानी पोषक द्रव ले जाने वाली नाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः गर्भनाल को दबाकर ठहर जाता है।
english: For her, on that account, Vāyu (Vāta), provoked, having seized Pitta and Śleṣman (Kapha), presses upon the fetus's rasa-carrying nāḍī (channel, probably the umbilical cord) and stays there.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 41 (tasyāḥ answers yasyāḥ). 'vāyu' is the wind-humour Vāta here. Reading nāḍī as the umbilical cord is probable, not stated by the word itself (nāḍī = vessel or channel). rasa = the first dhātu, nutrient fluid (doctrinal term, kept). 'garbhasya' is taken with nāḍī. pratipīḍya = pressing upon, obstructing; avatiṣṭhate = stays on.

hindi: तब दोषों से नाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः गर्भनाल के ढक जाने पर, जैसे नहर तिनकों और पत्तों आदि से ढक जाती है, रस के ठीक से न बहने के कारण गर्भ वृद्धि को न पाता हुआ बैठ जाता है या सूख जाता है।
english: Then, the nāḍī (probably the umbilical cord) being covered over by the doṣas, as a canal (kulyā) is by grass, leaves and the like, owing to the improper carrying of rasa the fetus does not attain growth, and settles down (upaviśati) or dries up (upaśuṣyati).
notes: The locative absolute is nāḍyāṃ ... praticchannāyām. upaviśati (sits down, settles) and upaśuṣyati (dries up) anticipate the names upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka used in the following units. The simile 'as a canal by grass, leaves and the like' is in the Sanskrit (kulyāyām iva). GROUPING: appears to continue 42 (tataḥ, 'then').

hindi: वहाँ जिस स्त्री में अनुमानित पाठ पर आर्तव यानी रज और परिस्राव कभी-कभी होते हैं और अल्प दिखाई देते हैं, और गर्भ माप से घटे बिना ही निरन्तर फड़कता है, तथा कुक्षि यानी पेट नहीं बढ़ता, उसे उपविष्टक कहते हैं। प्रामात् शब्द अस्पष्ट है और छोड़ा गया है।
english: Therein, in her in whom, on a conjectural reading, the ārtava (menstrual blood) and the flow (parisrāva) are occasional and are seen scanty, and the fetus constantly throbs (sphurati) without diminishing from the measure (parimāṇa), and the belly does not grow, that they call upaviṣṭaka. The word 'prāmāt' is unclear and left untranslated.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed ablative 'parisrāvāt' does not agree with the dual verb dṛśyete and dual 'alpau'; a nominative dual 'parisrāvāv alpau' (ārtava and flow, both scanty) fits, with v misread as d; compare 45, which sets 'monthly ārtava, daily flow, not very scanty' against this case
damaged or doubled: 'prāmāt' is not a known word and sits oddly before 'parimāṇāt' (perhaps a damaged pramāṇāt, 'from the standard measure'); kept unclear, not built on

notes: The printed text is doubtful in two places (see text_flags), so the translation is hedged ('on a conjectural reading') and 'prāmāt' is not translated. 'alpau' is a dual with no stated noun in the printed reading; the corrected reading makes it agree with ārtava and parisrāva. kādācitka = occasional. 'tam' is masculine: the condition or fetus is what they call upaviṣṭaka (not stated which). Orthographic normalisation recorded once here: vivarddhate -> vivardhate, arddha -> ardha (doubled consonant after r). The participle is printed aparihīyamāna with n, where the usual spelling after r is ṇ (parihīyamāṇa, as in 45); kept as printed.

hindi: जब प्रत्येक मास आर्तव या प्रतिदिन परिस्रवण बहुत थोड़ा न हो, और इस प्रकार क्षीण होता हुआ गर्भ देर से कुछ हिलता है।
english: When, however, there is ārtava (menstrual blood) every month or flow (parisravaṇa) every day, not very scanty, and so the fetus, wasting (parihīyamāṇa), moves a little after a long time.

text_flags.why: possible: 'garbhāś' (plural nominative) does not agree with the singular verb spandate; garbhaś is expected, so the long ā looks like a print slip

notes: Elliptical: the first clause has no verb (a copula 'is' is understood and not supplied). 'ca tathā' read as 'and so, and likewise'. This appears to be the second (milder) picture beside 44. parihīyamāṇa is the passive participle of pari-√hā, 'being diminished, wasting'. The text does not say here what condition is named; the names appear in 46. GROUPING: the 'yadā' clause appears to be completed in 46 ('tad upaśuṣkakaṃ nāgodaraṃ ca'); the sentence runs across the two units.

hindi: और कुक्षि यानी पेट बढ़ा हुआ होकर भी घटता है, वह उपशुष्कक है और नागोदर भी।

english: Those two, however, nourished by the slight tejas (vigour) of the mother's food, when they become well-nourished, then even after groups of years the woman (pramadā) gives birth indeed.
notes: 'tau' (dual) is read as the two kinds of fetus just described (upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka); the line does not name them. 'tejas' of food is kept as 'vigour'; it could also be read as 'essence'. varṣagaṇa = groups of years (a long time); no number is stated. 'prasūyate' is taken as the middle present, 'bears, gives birth'.

hindi: वहाँ वात से उपविष्टक और उपशुष्कक में वायु का प्रतिघात होता है यानी वह रुकता है; मल शब्द सहित, झागदार और टूटा हुआ निकलता है; मूत्र रुकता है; कमर, पीठ और हृदय में पीड़ा और जम्हाई होती है; नींद का नाश, बार-बार प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम, सूखी खाँसी और थकावट होती है; मानो दोनों कान भनभनाते हैं, मानो दोनों कनपटियाँ चुभती हैं; शरीर मानो चींटियों से जुड़ा हुआ है; मानो काटता हुआ वायु कुक्षि यानी पेट में घूमता है; मानो अन्धकार में प्रवेश कराया जाता है; अन्न का पाचन कठिनाई से होता है; दिन-प्रतिदिन हानि होती है; और त्वचा का फटा हुआ, विवर्ण और रूखा होना होता है।
english: Therein, in upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka, by Vāta, the vāyu is obstructed; dung (śakṛt) is passed noisy, frothy and broken; urine is held back; there are pain in the waist, back and heart (hṛdaya), and yawning; loss of sleep, repeated pratiśyāya (nasal catarrh), dry cough and lassitude (sāda); the two ears, as it were, hum, the two temples are, as it were, pricked; the body is, as it were, joined with ants; as if cutting about, vāyu wanders in the belly (kukṣi); one is, as it were, made to enter darkness (tamas); digestion of food is with difficulty; there is decline day after day; and there is the state of cracked, discoloured, rough skin.
notes: The construction 'vātena upaviṣṭakopaśuṣkakayoḥ' is loose (in these two, by Vāta); kept literal. 'abhīkṣṇam' may qualify nidrānāśa or pratiśyāya; placed with pratiśyāya. 'tamaḥ praveśa' (entering darkness) is a known symptom phrase (giddiness, blackout), probable. 'pipīlikābhir iva saṃsṛjyate' describes a crawling sensation, probable; kept literal. 'hṛdaya' = heart (standard); 'kaṭī' = waist or loins. pratiśyāya = nasal catarrh (standard). sāda = lassitude. The last compound ends in 'tvakttvaṃ' (doubled t is orthographic, tvak-tvam, recorded once here). The subject of 'bhavati' is the list of states; the woman is not named in this unit. Reading note: the printed Devanagari is तमइव (tama iva, regular sandhi with hiatus), so the word is iva 'as it were' (a simile like the others in the unit), not 'tamaiva'/'tamaḥ eva'; no text flag is needed. Whether 'tamaḥ praveśyate' means 'one is made to enter darkness' or 'darkness is brought on' is not settled by the wording.
lines_deva: तत्र वातेनोपविष्टकोपशुष्ककयोर्वायुः प्रतिहन्यते सशब्दं फेनिलं विच्छिन्नं शकृदुपवेश्यते मूत्रमुपरुध्यते कटीपृष्ठहृदयेषु वेदनाजृंभा निद्रानाशोऽभीक्ष्णं प्रतिश्यायः शुष्ककासः सादः क्ष्वेलेते इवकर्णौ तुद्येते इव शंखौ पिपीलिकाभिरिव संसृज्यते शरीरं परिकृंतन्निव वायुर्भ्रमति कुक्षौ तमइव प्रवेश्यते दुःखेनान्नस्य जरणमहरहः परिहानिः स्फुटितविवर्णपरुषत्वक्त्त्वं च भवति
lines_iast: tatra vātenopaviṣṭakopaśuṣkakayorvāyuḥ pratihanyate saśabdaṃ phenilaṃ vicchinnaṃ śakṛdupaveśyate mūtramuparudhyate kaṭīpṛṣṭhahṛdayeṣu vedanājṛṃbhā nidrānāśo'bhīkṣṇaṃ pratiśyāyaḥ śuṣkakāsaḥ sādaḥ kṣvelete ivakarṇau tudyete iva śaṃkhau pipīlikābhiriva saṃsṛjyate śarīraṃ parikṛṃtanniva vāyurbhramati kukṣau tamaiva praveśyate duḥkhenānnasya jaraṇamaharahaḥ parihāniḥ sphuṭitavivarṇaparuṣatvakttvaṃ ca bhavati

hindi: पित्त से ताम्र-हरित निकलता है; धूमिक और अम्लक, जिनका अर्थ अनिश्चित है; वमन, मूर्च्छा, कुक्षि और हृदय में जलन; आँखों, मूत्र और नखों का पीले, लाल और गोमूत्र की आभा वाले होना; और स्त्री काली, दुर्बल और नित्य पीड़ा वाली हो जाती है।
english: By Pitta, a coppery-green (one) is passed; dhūmika and amlaka (words of uncertain sense, 'smoky' and 'sour'); vomiting (chardi); fainting (mūrcchā); burning in the belly and heart (hṛdaya); the state of the eyes, urine and nails being yellow, red and cow-urine-hued; and the woman becomes dark (kālī), weak and constantly in pain (śūla).
notes: Elliptical: the noun of 'tāmraharitam' is not stated; śakṛt (dung) of 48 is the likely understood noun and is not supplied. 'dhūmika' and 'amlaka' are kept untranslated in sense: they may be a smoky and a sour sensation or taste, but this is not firm. 'pīta-rakta-gomūtrābha' may also be read as 'yellow-red, or cow-urine-hued'; the plainer list is kept. 'tva' is the abstract on the whole list of netra, mūtra, nakha. mūrcchā = fainting (standard).

hindi: श्लेष्मा यानी कफ से: मुख की मधुरता, उत्क्लेश यानी मिचली, कफ का उगलना, भोजन से द्वेष, हाथ, पैर और आँखों का श्वेत होना, खाँसी और श्वास यानी साँस फूलना।

notes: Elliptical: no verb, as in 49 (the list continues the Vāta and Pitta pictures of 48-49). utkleśa = nausea (standard). 'śleṣmodvamana' = bringing up phlegm; the print gives no word for 'vomiting' other than udvamana. śvāsa = laboured breathing (asthma-type, probable), kept as breathlessness.

english: Likewise, (the use) of milks (payas), rasas (juices or broths) and āmagarbhas (literally 'raw fetuses'; exact sense uncertain) is promoting the growth of the fetus.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'viddhi' (piercing) makes no sense here; vṛddhi (growth) is needed after 'garbha', in line with 47 and 59-60, and ṛ misread as i is a plausible print slip

notes: Elliptical: the masculine 'karaḥ' agrees with 'upayogaḥ' of 51, which is understood and shown in parentheses in English only. 'rasa' here may mean meat-broth or other juices; not settled. 'āmagarbha' (raw/unripe fetus or embryo) is kept as printed; the text does not say whose, and the sense is not enriched. It recurs in 63.
lines_deva: तथा पयसां रसानामामगर्भाणां च गर्भविद्धिकरः

hindi: वैसे ही इन्हीं घृत आदि के साथ भोजन कराना।
english: Likewise, feeding (saṃbhojana) with these very (ones), with ghee and the others.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. 'etaiḥ ... ghṛtādibhiḥ': the nouns are not stated; 'these very ones' is read as ghee and the like. The recipient of the feeding is not stated (the woman is the natural reading).
lines_deva: तथा संभोजनमेतैरेव च घृतादिभिः

words.gloss: carriage, riding; vehicle, conveyance; and others
shaking, jolting; rubbing, wiping; yawning, stretching

hindi: भली-भाँति भोजन पाने वाली का बार-बार यान, वाहन आदि से, तथा क्षोभण यानी हिलाने, मार्जन यानी रगड़ने और जृम्भण यानी जम्हाई से उपपादन।
english: Of one well provided with food (subhikṣā), repeatedly, the bringing about (upapādana) by means of carriages, vehicles and the like, and by shaking (kṣobhaṇa), rubbing (mārjana) and yawning (jṛmbhaṇa).
notes: The sense is not firm. 'subhikṣāyāḥ' (of a woman with plentiful food) is taken with the woman understood; the object of 'upapādanam' is not stated; and whether the instrumentals 'kṣobhaṇa-mārjana-jṛmbhaṇaiḥ' are means of the bringing about (parallel to 'yānavāhanādibhiḥ') or what is brought about is open. Elliptical: no verb. mārjana can mean wiping or rubbing; jṛmbhaṇa yawning or stretching.
lines_deva: सुभिक्षाया अभीक्ष्णं यानवाहनादिभिः क्षोभणमार्जनजृंभणैरुपपादनं

hindi: फिर विशेष रूप से वात में पहले ही सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से युक्त दूध की बस्ति यानी एनिमा देकर, ठंडे जल से नहाई हुई को मृदु शालि का भात खिलाए।
english: Then, especially in Vāta, first of all, having given a milk-basti (enema) provided with saindhava (rock salt), one should feed her, bathed in cold water, soft boiled śāli rice (śāli-odana).

text_flags.why: near certain: 'strāta' is not a word; snāta (bathed) is needed, st for sn is a plausible print slip (the same in 80)
possible: the absolutive of √dā is dattvā; 'datvā' with one t looks like a print habit or slip

notes: basti = enema here (a milk enema, given with the salt). 'her' is the accusative feminine 'snātām' (the woman is understood). 'mṛdu' is taken with the rice (soft). 'viśeṣeṇa vāte' = especially in the Vāta case. śāli = a winter rice (standard); odana = boiled rice.
lines_deva: अथ विशेषेण वाते पूर्वमेव सैंधवोपहितं क्षीरबस्तिं दत्वा शीतोदकस्त्रातां मृदु शाल्योदनं भोजयेत्
lines_iast: atha viśeṣeṇa vāte pūrvameva saiṃdhavopahitaṃ kṣīrabastiṃ datvā śītodakastrātāṃ mṛdu śālyodanaṃ bhojayet

words.gloss: vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa, probable); and the others; group (gaṇa); prepared

hindi: फिर विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द आदि के समूह से तैयार किए घी से अनुवासन यानी चिकनाई वाली बस्ति दे।
english: Then one should give an anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with ghee (sarpis) prepared with the vidārī-and-others group (vidārī-ādi-gaṇa; vidārī probably Indian kudzu, Pueraria tuberosa).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 55 (Vāta case). vidārī: Pueraria tuberosa (probable); the members of the vidārī-ādi group are not listed here. anuvāsayet: an anuvāsana is an oil or ghee enema (standard), kept as 'give an anuvāsana'. sādhita = prepared (glossary).
lines_deva: ततो विदार्यादिगणसाधितेन सर्पिषा ऽनुवासयेत्

hindi: और निवात यानी वायु से बचाव का सेवन करे।
english: And one should resort to shelter from the wind (nivāta).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 55-56. nivāta (n.) = wind-sheltered state or place; not enriched.
lines_deva: निवातं च सेवेत

words.gloss: madhuka (licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, probable); vidārī (see 56); decoction (niryūha); cooked

hindi: पित्त में मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द के निर्यूह यानी काढ़े से पकाया हुआ दूध पिए।
english: In Pitta, one should drink milk cooked with a decoction (niryūha) of madhuka (probably licorice) and vidārī (probably Indian kudzu).
notes: madhuka = licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra), probable; the word can also mean the mahua tree (Madhuca longifolia), so it is hedged. niryūha = decoction; siddha = cooked. 'cooked with a decoction' is read as milk prepared with the decoction.
lines_deva: पित्ते मधुकविदारीनिर्यूहसिद्धं पयः पिबेत

words.gloss: husked, without husk; māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo, standard); āḍhaka (a measure)
in a mortar (udūkhala, variant of ulūkhala)
tittiri (partridge, probable); kapiñjala (a game bird, commonly francolin or partridge; identity disputed); either; rasa (broth)
words.gram: dvandva + tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg. (anyātara corrected to anyatara)

words.gloss: upaviṣṭaka; increase; for the sake of
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used as ind.

words.gloss: upaśuṣkaka; growth; for the sake of
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used as ind. (printed vṛdvy-)

hindi: तीन मोटी कुक्कुटियों यानी मुर्गियों और आढक भर छिलका उतारे माष यानी उड़द को दूध और जल के साथ ओखली में कूटकर, उसके रस तथा घी के साथ तित्तिरी यानी सम्भवतः तीतर या कपिञ्जल, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, में से किसी एक का रस पकाकर, उपविष्टक की वृद्धि के लिए और उपशुष्कक की वृद्धि के लिए पिलाए।
english: Having crushed in a mortar, with milk and water, three large hens (kukkuṭī, fowl) and an āḍhaka (a measure) of husked māṣa (black gram), and having prepared, with its rasa and with ghee, the rasa (broth) of either tittiri (probably partridge) or kapiñjala (a game bird, identity disputed), one should make (her) drink it, for the increase of upaviṣṭaka and for the growth of upaśuṣkaka.

text_flags.why: possible: the absolutive of √kṣud (to crush) is saṃkṣudya; the aspirate dh looks like a print slip
near certain: anyatara (either) has short a; 'anyātara' is a print slip
near certain: 'vṛdvyartham' for vṛddhy-artham; dv for ddh is a recorded OCR confusion

notes: The grammar of the middle of the sentence is loose: what is cooked with 'its rasa and ghee' is the rasa of tittiri or kapiñjala (as translated), but the crushed mass and its juice could also be cooked together with it; kept as printed. 'tad-rasena' = with the rasa of that (the crushed mass). 'pāyayet' = should make (her) drink; 'it' is understood. sthūla-kukkuṭī = large hen; kukkuṭa = fowl (glossary). āḍhaka is a measure; its size is not given here. udūkhala is an accepted variant of ulūkhala (mortar). tittiri = partridge (probable); kapiñjala = a francolin or partridge-type bird, disputed. Identification of māṣa: Vigna mungo (standard).
lines_deva: तिस्रः स्थूलकुक्कुटीर्निस्तुषमाषाढकं च क्षीरोदकेनोदूखले संक्षुध्य तद्रसेन सर्पिषा च तित्तिरिकपिंजलान्यातररसं साधयित्वा पाययेदुपविष्टकविवर्द्धनार्थमुपशुष्ककवृद्व्यर्थं च
lines_iast: tisraḥ sthūlakukkuṭīrnistuṣamāṣāḍhakaṃ ca kṣīrodakenodūkhale saṃkṣudhya tadrasena sarpiṣā ca tittirikapiṃjalānyātararasaṃ sādhayitvā pāyayedupaviṣṭakavivarddhanārthamupaśuṣkakavṛdvyarthaṃ ca

words.gram: inst. pl. (the ending -yaiḥ is printed in the next token)
ind. (printed yaiśca, with the ending of the previous word)

hindi: बकरी के घी, दूध और जीवनीय यानी जीवन देने वालों से तैयार की गई गाढ़ी लपसी यानी यवागू पिए।
english: One should drink a yavāgū (thick gruel) prepared with goat ghee, with milk, and with the jīvanīya (life-promoting) (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: the printed space splits jīvanīyaiḥ ca into 'jīvanī' and 'yaiśca'; the relative 'yaiḥ' has no matching 'taiḥ', so the joined jīvanīyaiḥ ca is read

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the remedies of 59. The two printed tokens 'jīvanī' and 'yaiśca' are read as one word jīvanīyaiḥ plus ca; the whole word is given on the first token. 'ajā-sarpis' = ghee of the she-goat. jīvanīya = life-promoting drugs (a class; not listed here). yavāgū = thick gruel (glossary).
lines_deva: अजासर्पिषा क्षीरेण जीवनी यैश्च संस्कृतां यवागूं पिबेत
lines_iast: ajāsarpiṣā kṣīreṇa jīvanī yaiśca saṃskṛtāṃ yavāgūṃ pibeta

words.gloss: payasyā (a plant, identity disputed; candidates include Ipomoea digitata and Pueraria tuberosa)
words.gram: f., first member of the compound that follows

words.gloss: kākolī (identity disputed; candidates include Roscoea purpurea and Fritillaria roylei); pair; suniṣaṇṇaka (Marsilea minuta or M. quadrifolia, probable); paste (kalka)

hindi: पयस्या, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है और जो क्षीरविदारी या विदारीकन्द हो सकती है, काकोली का जोड़ा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और सुनिषण्णक यानी सम्भवतः चौपतिया की लुगदी तथा दूध के साथ घी पकाए।
english: One should cook ghee with milk and with a paste (kalka) of payasyā (identity disputed), the pair of kākolī (identity disputed) and suniṣaṇṇaka (probably Marsilea).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 60. payasyā: identity disputed (candidates include kṣīravidārī, Ipomoea digitata, and Pueraria tuberosa). kākolī-dvaya: 'the pair of kākolī' (the two members are not named in this line); identity disputed. suniṣaṇṇaka: Marsilea (probable). 'payasyā' is read as the first member of the list in apposition with the compound, not as a separate nominative.
lines_deva: पयस्या काकोलीद्वयसुनिषण्णककल्केन पयसा च सर्पिर्विपचेत्

hindi: उससे दूध के अनुपान के साथ उपयोग करे।
english: With that, one should take (it), having milk as the after-drink (anupāna).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 61 ('tena' is taken as the ghee of 61). The object of 'upayuñjīta' is not stated. 'kṣīrānupānam' is read as adverbial (with milk as after-drink); anupāna = a liquid taken after the dose.
lines_deva: तेन क्षीरानुपानमुपयुंजीत

words.gloss: raw, unripe; fetus, embryo (āmagarbha; exact sense uncertain); rasa (broth, juice)
words.gram: karmadhāraya + tat-puruṣa, m. inst. sg. (printed rāsena)

hindi: या आमगर्भ यानी कच्चे गर्भ, जिसका ठीक अर्थ अनिश्चित है, के रस के साथ खाए।
english: Or one should eat with the rasa (broth) of āmagarbha (literally 'raw fetus'; exact sense uncertain).

text_flags.why: near certain: 'rāsa' is not a word here; rasa (broth, juice) fits, as in 52 and the other 'rasena' units

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 60-62 as a further remedy. The printed avagraha in vā'śnīyāt is vā + aśnīyāt. 'āmagarbha' recurs from 52 and is not enriched (it could mean raw embryos of animals, or eggs; not stated). 'eat with' keeps the instrumental of the Sanskrit; the food eaten is not stated.
lines_deva: आमगर्भरासेन वाऽश्नीयात्

words.gloss: gṛdhra (vulture); first member of a damaged compound

hindi: और वहाँ उन्हीं को; और अनुमानित पाठ पर गृध्र यानी गिद्ध, एक अस्पष्ट शब्द, और जलचर यानी जल में चलने वालों के मांस।
english: And those very (ones) there; and, on a conjectural reading, flesh of vulture (gṛdhra), (one word unclear), and of water-movers (jalacara).

text_flags.why: possible: the hyphen after 'gṛdhra-' and the odd fragment 'abhyeṃ' show damage; the compound is incomplete and the middle part cannot be restored

notes: The printed compound 'gṛdhra- abhyeṃjalacaramāṃsāni' is damaged. Only the clear parts are shown, hedged: gṛdhra (vulture), jalacara (moving in water; a general term for water animals) and māṃsa (flesh). 'abhyeṃ' is left unclear. 'tān eva' (those very, masculine plural) has no clear antecedent in this unit; it may refer to the rasa or meats of the preceding units. GROUPING: appears to continue 60-63. Low confidence.
lines_deva: तानेव च तत्र गृध्र- अभ्येंजलचरमांसानि च
lines_iast: tāneva ca tatra gṛdhra- abhyeṃjalacaramāṃsāni ca

words.gloss: meat (piśita); first part of upadaṃśa, continued in the next token

words.gram: damaged compound member, n. acc. sg.

words.gloss: equal (sama); night (read as sapta-rātram, 'seven nights', on a conjectural reading)

hindi: कफ में तो साफ सुरा यानी मादक पेय, मांस को साथ खाने की वस्तु बनाकर, तीन रात, अस्पष्ट संख्या की रात, या अनुमानित पाठ पर सात रात पिए। आम्रोदक शब्द अस्पष्ट है और छोड़ा गया है।
english: In Kapha, however, one should drink clear surā (an intoxicating drink), with meat as its relish, for three nights, for an unclear number of nights, or, on a conjectural reading, for seven nights. The word 'āmrodaka' is unclear and left untranslated.

text_flags.why: possible: 'samarātra' (equal night) gives no sense in a list of numbered nights; pta misread as ma is a recorded OCR confusion
damaged: the leading numeral (and the preceding word) are lost; only the fragment '-rātram' is printed
damaged or unknown: 'āmrodaka' is not a known word here (perhaps āmra-udaka, but the sense is not firm); left untranslated and unclear

notes: Damaged unit. 'tvāmrodaka' = tu + a word 'āmrodaka' (perhaps āmra-udaka, but the sense is not firm); not translated. 'piśitopa daṃśām' is printed with a space: read as piśita-upadaṃśām (spacing slip, no flag). accha = clear (of surā). 'pibet' has surā as its object. Low confidence because of the damaged words and the conjectured 'seven'.
lines_deva: कफे त्वाम्रोदक पिशितोप दंशामच्छसुरां त्रिरात्रं -रात्रं समरात्रं वा पिबेत्
lines_iast: kaphe tvāmrodaka piśitopa daṃśāmacchasurāṃ trirātraṃ -rātraṃ samarātraṃ vā pibet

words.gloss: tila (sesame, Sesamum indicum, standard); mudga (mung bean, Vigna radiata, standard); māṣa (black gram); lavaṇa (salt); bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos, standard); leaf (patra)

hindi: तिल, मूँग, माष यानी उड़द, लवण और बिल्व यानी बेल के पत्तों, इन पाँच के साथ घी का पात्र मिलाकर, भली-भाँति सुरक्षित रखवाए।
english: Having combined a pātra (vessel-full) of ghee with the five: sesame (tila), mung bean (mudga), black gram (māṣa), salt (lavaṇa) and bilva (bael) leaves (patra), one should have (it) put away, well guarded.
notes: 'pañcabhiḥ' (five) matches the five items tila, mudga, māṣa, lavaṇa, bilva-patra, so 'bilvapatra' is read as one item. 'ghṛtapātra' is a vessel-full of ghee; whether pātra is a fixed measure is not stated (it recurs in 68). 'svanuguptam' = su-anuguptam, well protected. Identifications: tila, mudga, bilva standard.
lines_deva: तिलमुद्गमाषलवणबिल्वपत्रैः पंचभिर्घृतपात्रं संयोज्य स्वनुगुप्तं निधापयेत्

hindi: फिर प्रातः बिल्व यानी बेल के आकार का पिण्ड, उबाले हुए ठंडे बकरी के दूध के अनुपान के साथ, खाए।
english: Then, in the morning, one should eat a lump (piṇḍa) of the size of a bilva (bael), with boiled, cooled goat's milk as the after-drink (anupāna).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 66 (the piṇḍa is presumably the combined ghee mixture; not stated). 'bilvamātra' = of the measure of a bilva (fruit); kept as 'size of a bilva'. śṛta = boiled (glossary). anupāna = liquid taken after.
lines_deva: ततः प्रातः पिंडं बिल्वमात्रं शृतशीतच्छागदुग्धानुपानं प्राश्नीयात्
lines_iast: tataḥ prātaḥ piṃḍaṃ bilvamātraṃ śṛtaśītacchāgadugdhānupānaṃ prāśnīyāt

words.gloss: jujube (badara, Ziziphus jujuba, standard); powder; vessel-full (pātra)

hindi: या यहीं बेर के चूर्ण का पात्र भी रखे।
english: Or, right here, one should also put a pātra of badara (jujube) powder.

text_flags.why: possible: 'nidaṣyāt' is not a form; ni-√dhā optative is nidadhyāt, and dhy misread as ṣy is a plausible print slip (compare nidhāpayet in 66)

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 66-67. 'atra eva' = 'in this very (mixture or case)'; the noun is not stated. The sense of the verb on the corrected reading is 'put in'; the measure 'pātra' as in 66.
lines_deva: अत्रैव वा बदरचूर्णपात्रमपि निदष्यात्

words.gloss: when there is no growth, in non-growth

hindi: इस प्रकार वृद्धि न होने पर तीक्ष्णों से विरेचन कराए और अपरा यानी जेर को गिराने वालों से गिराए।
english: Thus, when there is no growth, one should purge with sharp (ones), and should cause (it) to fall with those that cause the aparā (placenta) to fall.
notes: GROUPING: appears to close the remedies of 59-68 for the non-growth cases. The object of 'pātayet' is not stated. aparā = placenta (standard); 'aparā-pātanīya' = what causes the aparā to fall (drugs of the placenta-expelling kind); the Sanskrit gives no names. tīkṣṇa = sharp, strong; the nouns are not stated.
lines_deva: एवमवृद्धौ तीक्ष्णैर्विरेचयेदपरापातनीयैश्च पातयेत्

words.gloss: pramuma (unclear; read as pramūḍha, 'stupefied', on a conjectural reading)

hindi: किन्तु जिस स्त्री के स्रोतस यानी शरीर के मार्ग वात से ग्रस्त हों, उसका चिपका हुआ गर्भ अनुमानित पाठ पर मूढ़ होकर हिलता नहीं; उसे लीन कहते हैं।
english: Of her, however, whose channels (srotas) are afflicted by Vāta, the fetus, clinging (saṃlīna) and, on a conjectural reading, stupefied, does not move; that they call līna.

text_flags.why: possible: srotas is neuter, nominative plural srotāṃsi; the missing anusvara looks like a print slip
possible: 'pramuma' is not a known word; pramūḍha (stupefied, inert) fits 'does not move', and the Devanagari ढ is easily misread as म

notes: The reading 'pramumaḥ' is doubtful, so the translation is hedged. The relative clause 'yasyāḥ ... srotāṃsi' gives the condition; 'tam' (masculine) takes the fetus or condition as what is called līna (not stated which). srotas = body channel (doctrinal term, kept with a plain gloss). 'upasṛṣṭa' = touched, afflicted. līna = clinging, hidden, not further enriched.
lines_deva: यस्याः पुनर्वातोपसृष्टस्रोतासि संलीनो गर्भः प्रमुमो न स्पंदते तं लीनमित्याहुः
lines_iast: yasyāḥ punarvātopasṛṣṭasrotāsi saṃlīno garbhaḥ pramumo na spaṃdate taṃ līnamityāhuḥ

words.gloss: hawk (śyena, probable); osprey (utkrośa, probable); cow (go); fish (matsya); monitor lizard (godha, standard); peacock (śikhin, standard); fowl (kukkuṭa); partridge (tittirī, probable)
red; śāli rice (Oryza sativa, standard); boiled rice (odana)

hindi: वहाँ श्येन यानी सम्भवतः बाज, उत्क्रोश यानी सम्भवतः कुरर, गाय, मछली, गोधा यानी गोह, शिखी यानी मोर, कुक्कुट यानी मुर्गा और तित्तिरी यानी सम्भवतः तीतर में से किसी एक के बहुत घी वाले रस से, या घी से भरपूर माष यानी उड़द के यूष यानी सूप या मूली के यूष से, लाल शालि का भात खिलाए।
english: In that case, one should feed (her) red śāli rice (rakta-śāli-odana) with the rasa (broth) of any one of probably hawk (śyena), probably osprey (utkrośa), cow (go), fish (matsya), monitor lizard (godha), peacock (śikhin), fowl (kukkuṭa) and probably partridge (tittirī), made with abundant ghee, or with a māṣa-yūṣa (black-gram soup) or a mūlaka-yūṣa (radish soup) rich in ghee.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 70 (the līna case). The eight names are read as: śyena, utkrośa, go, matsya, godha, śikhin, kukkuṭa, tittirī; 'go' is taken as cow (it could be a short form of another name, but cow is the plain sense). Animal identifications: śyena = hawk or falcon (probable), utkrośa = osprey (probable), godha = monitor lizard (standard), śikhin = peacock (standard), tittirī = partridge (probable). 'bhūrisarpiṣkeṇa' is taken with the rasa and 'ghṛtāḍhyena' with the two soups, but both could qualify all; kept as the plain reading. yūṣa = strained soup. The object of bhojayet (the woman) is not stated.
lines_deva: तत्र श्येनोत्क्रोशगोमत्स्यगोधशिखिकुक्कुटतित्तिरीणामन्यतमस्य रसेन भूरिसर्पिष्केण माषयूषेण मूलकयूषेण वा घृताढ्येन रक्तशाल्योदनं भोजयेत्
lines_iast: tatra śyenotkrośagomatsyagodhaśikhikukkuṭatittirīṇāmanyatamasya rasena bhūrisarpiṣkeṇa māṣayūṣeṇa mūlakayūṣeṇa vā ghṛtāḍhyena raktaśālyodanaṃ bhojayet

words.gloss: sesame; black gram; bilva (bael); śalāṭu (unripe fruit); combined with

hindi: या तिल, माष यानी उड़द, बिल्व यानी बेल और शलाटु यानी कच्चे फल से युक्त सक्तु यानी भुने अन्न का आटा दूध के साथ पिलाए।
english: Or one should make (her) drink saktu (flour of roasted grain) combined with sesame, black gram, bilva (bael) and śalāṭu (unripe fruit), with milk.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 70-71. The list may also be read with 'bilva-śalāṭu' as one item (unripe bilva fruit); the four-member reading is the literal one. saktu: the grain is not stated (barley is usual but not said). 'pāyayet' is the literal 'should make drink'.
lines_deva: सक्तून्वा तिलमाषबिल्वशलाटुयुक्तान् पयसा पाययेत्

hindi: या सम्भवतः चर्बीयुक्त मांस को साथ खाने की वस्तु बनाकर मार्द्वीक यानी अंगूर की मदिरा।
english: Or mārdvīka (grape wine), having meat that is probably fatty (medya) as its relish.

text_flags.why: near certain: mārdvīka (from mṛdvīkā, grape); dv misread as ddh is a recorded OCR confusion (mṛdvīkānāṃ is printed correctly in 79)

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 72. Elliptical: the verb 'pāyayet' of 72 is carried and not supplied. 'medya' is taken as 'fatty' (probable); it could also be read medhya (intellect-promoting), which does not suit meat well. upadaṃśa = relish or bite eaten with a drink.
lines_deva: मेद्यमांसोपदंशं वा मार्द्दीकं

words.gloss: belly (udara); groin (vaṅkṣaṇa); thigh (ūru); waist (kaṭī); flank (pārśva); back (pṛṣṭha)
should anoint, should rub with oil

hindi: और तेल से बार-बार पेट, वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़, ऊरु यानी जाँघों, कमर, पार्श्व यानी बगल और पीठ का अभ्यंग करे।
english: And one should repeatedly anoint, with oil, the belly (udara), groin (vaṅkṣaṇa), thighs (ūru), waist (kaṭī), flanks (pārśva) and back (pṛṣṭha).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 70-73. taila = oil (the kind is not stated). vaṅkṣaṇa = groin (standard).
lines_deva: तैलेन चाभीक्ष्णमुदरवंक्षणोरुकटीपार्श्वपृष्ठान्यभ्यंज्यात्

hindi: और इसे बार-बार हर्षित करे।
english: And one should gladden her again and again.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 74. harṣayet (causative of √hṛṣ): 'gladden, cheer'; the plainest sense is kept.
lines_deva: मुहुर्मुहुश्चैनां हर्षयेत्

hindi: और पहले कहे हुए पर दृष्टि रखे।
english: And one should look to what was said before.
notes: GROUPING: appears to close the līna treatment of 70-75. What 'pūrvoktam' refers to (the earlier regimen) is not stated in the line.
lines_deva: पूर्वोक्तं चेक्षेत

words.gloss: udāvarta (reversed, upward course of Vāta; standard); vibandha (constipation)
words.gram: compound, m. nom. sg. (dvandva or tat-puruṣa; see notes)

hindi: जिसे फिर उदावर्त यानी वात का उलटा ऊपर चढ़ना और विबन्ध यानी कब्ज हो, उसका वात हरने वाले चिकने अन्न और पेयों से उपचार करे।
english: Of her, however, who may have udāvarta (a disorder in which Vāta runs upward) and vibandha (constipation), one should treat her with Vāta-removing, unctuous foods and drinks.
notes: A new topic appears to begin here. 'udāvarta-vibandhaḥ' is read as two disorders (dvandva); it can also be read 'constipation of the udāvarta kind'. 'vāta-hara' modifies the foods and drinks together with 'snigdha'. udāvarta printed with rtt (orthographic, recorded once in 44-glossary style).
lines_deva: यस्याः पुनरुदावर्त्तविबंधः स्यात्तां वातहरस्निग्धान्नपानैरुपाचरेत्

words.gloss: madhuraka (probably a group of sweet drugs; members not listed); cooked

hindi: आठवें मास में तो मधुरक यानी सम्भवतः मधुर औषधों के समूह से पकाए तेल से अनुवासन यानी चिकनाई वाली बस्ति दे।
english: In the eighth month, however, one should give an anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with oil cooked with madhuraka (probably a group of sweet drugs).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 77. 'the eighth month' is understood as of pregnancy; the unit does not say so. madhuraka: a drug or group named madhuraka; 'a group of sweet drugs' is probable, not certain (disputed), and the members are not listed here.
lines_deva: अष्टमे तु मासे मधुरकसिद्धेन तैलेनानुवासयेत्

words.gloss: vīraṇa (a fragrant grass, Vetiveria zizanioides, probable); śāli (rice, Oryza sativa, standard); kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata, standard); kāśa (Saccharum spontaneum, standard); ikṣuvālikā (identity disputed); vetasa (cane or willow, identity disputed); parivyādha (unidentified); roots (mūla)
words.gram: dvandva + tat-puruṣa, n. gen. pl. (printed ikṣubālikā, veetasa)

words.gloss: bhūtikā (unidentified); ananta (on a conjectural reading; sārivā, Hemidesmus indicus, probable); kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea, standard); parūṣaka (Grewia asiatica, standard); madhuka (licorice, see 58); mṛdvīkā (grape, Vitis vinifera, standard)
piyāla (Buchanania lanzan, probable); bibhītaka (Terminalia bellirica, standard); kernel (majjā); sesame (tila); paste (kalka); combined with

hindi: उसके सिद्ध न होने पर वीरण यानी सम्भवतः खस की घास, शालि यानी धान, कुश यानी कुशा घास, काश यानी काँस, इक्षुवालिका, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, वेतस, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और परिव्याध, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, इनकी जड़ों का, तथा भूतिका, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, अनुमानित पाठ पर अनन्त यानी सम्भवतः सारिवा, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, परूषक यानी फालसा, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और मृद्वीका यानी अंगूर का, दूध और आधे जल के साथ रस निकालकर, उससे, पियाल यानी सम्भवतः चिरौंजी और बिभीतक यानी बहेड़े की गिरी तथा तिल की लुगदी से युक्त, थोड़े नमकीन और गरम रस से निरूह दे।
english: If that does not succeed, having extracted, with milk and half water, the rasa (decoction) of the roots of vīraṇa (probably vetiver grass), śāli (rice), kuśa (kusha grass), kāśa (kans grass), ikṣuvālikā (identity disputed), vetasa (identity disputed) and parivyādha (unidentified), and of bhūtikā (unidentified), ananta (on a conjectural reading; probably sārivā), kāśmarya (gmelina), parūṣaka (phalsa), madhuka (probably licorice) and mṛdvīkā (grape), one should give a nirūha (decoction enema) with that, combined with a paste (kalka) of the kernels (majjā) of piyāla (probably Buchanania) and bibhītaka and of sesame (tila), slightly salty and warm.

text_flags.why: near certain for veetasa -> vetasa (stray e); ikṣubālikā for ikṣuvālikā is the usual v/b interchange of this print
possible: stray anusvāras (bhūtikāṃ ... naṃta) for bhūtikā-ananta-kāśmarya; the reading 'ananta' is conjectural

notes: A long list, read as two groups. 'mūlānām' is taken with the first group (roots); the second group stands in the genitive without 'mūla' and may be whole drugs or roots, not settled. 'ikṣubālikā' is read as one name (ikṣuvālikā, v/b interchange). Identifications: vīraṇa probable (the grass whose root is uśīra), kuśa, kāśa, śāli, kāśmarya, parūṣaka, mṛdvīkā, bibhītaka standard; ananta probable but hedged because the reading is conjectural; piyāla probable (Buchanania lanzan); ikṣuvālikā and vetasa disputed; parivyādha and bhūtikā unidentified. majjā = kernel (glossary). 'tad-asiddhau' = if that (the anuvāsana) does not succeed, taken from the context. nirūha = decoction enema (standard); the rasa is the extract. The grammar 'tena ... yuktena ... nirūhayet' puts the paste in the extract.
lines_deva: तदसिद्धौवीरणशालिकुशकाशेक्षुबालिकावेेतसपरिव्याधमूलानां भूतिकांनंतकाश्मर्यपरूषकमधुकमृद्वीकानां च पयसाऽर्द्धोदकेनोद्धृत्य रसं तेन पियालबिभीतकमज्जतिलकल्कयुक्तेनेषल्लवणोष्णेन निरूहयेत्

hindi: और जिसका विबन्ध यानी कब्ज दूर हो गया हो, जो नहा चुकी और खा चुकी हो, उसे सायंकाल उसी तेल से अनुवासन दे।
english: And, her whose constipation (vibandha) has gone, who has bathed and eaten, one should give in the evening an anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with that very oil.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'strāta' is not a word; snāta (bathed) fits, as in 55

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 78-79. 'tena eva tailena' = the oil of 78 (madhuraka-cooked oil); that identification follows from the context and is not stated. aśita = having eaten.
lines_deva: विगतविबंधां च स्त्राताशितां सायं तेनैव तैलेनानुवासयेत्
lines_iast: vigatavibaṃdhāṃ ca strātāśitāṃ sāyaṃ tenaiva tailenānuvāsayet
